record.reference: Shepherd of Hermas — Similitude 5, section v

source.text: Εἶπόν σοι, φησί, καὶ ἄρτι, ὅτι πανοῦργος εἶ καὶ αὐθάδης, ἐπερωτῶν τὰς ἐπιλύσεις τῶν παραβολῶν. ἐπειδὴ δὲ οὕτω παράμονος εἶ, ἐπιλύσω σοι τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ ἀγροῦ καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν τῶν ἀκο αὐτοὺς τοῦ συντηρεῖν αὐτούς· καὶ αὐτὸς τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν ἐκαθάρισε πολλὰ κοπιάσας καὶ πολλοὺς κόπους ἠντληκώς· οὐδεὶς γὰρ δύναται σκαφεῦσαι ἄτερ κόπου ἢ μόχθου. 3. αὐτὸς οὖν καθαρίσας τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς τρίβους τῆς ζωῆς, δοὺς αὐτοῖς τὸν νόμον ὃν ἔλαβε παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ. 4. βλέπεις, φησίν, ὅτι αὐτὸς κύριός ἐστι τοῦ λαοῦ, ἐξουσίαν πᾶσαν λαβὼν παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ. ὅτι δὲ ὁ κύριος σύμβουλον ἔλαβε τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἐνδόξους ἀγγέλους περὶ τῆς κληρονομίας τοῦ δούλου, ἄκουε. 5. τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ προόν, τὸ κτίσαν πᾶσαν τὴν κτίσιν, κατῴκισεν ὁ Θεὸς εἰς σάρκα ἣν ἠβούλετο. αὕτη οὖν ἡ σάρξ, ἐν ᾗ κατῴκησε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἐδούλευσε τῷ πνεύματι καλῶς ἐν σεμνότητι καὶ ἁγνείᾳ πορευθεῖσα, μηδὲν ὅλως μιάνασα τὸ πνεῦμα. 6. πολιτευσαμένην οὖν αὐτὴν καλῶς καὶ ἁγνῶς καὶ συγκοπιάσασαν τῷ πνεύματι καὶ συνεργήσασαν ἐν παντὶ πράγματι, ἰσχυρῶς καὶ ἀνδρείως ἀναστραφεῖσαν, μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου εἵλατο κοινωνόν· ἤρεσε γὰρ [τῷ Κυρίῳ] ἡ πορεία τῆς σαρκὸς ταύτης, ὅτι οὐκ ἐμιάνθη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔχουσα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον. 7. σύμβουλον οὖν ἔλαβε τὸν υἱὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοὺς ἐνδόξους, ἵνα καὶ ἡ σὰρξ αὕτη, δουλεύσασα τῷ πνεύματι ἀμέμπτως, σχῇ τόπον τινὰ κατασκηνώσεως, καὶ μὴ δόξῃ τὸν μισθὸν τῆς δουλείας αὐτῆς ἀπολωλεκέναι· πᾶσα γὰρ σὰρξ ἀπολήψεται μισθὸν ἡ εὑρεθεῖσα ἀμίαντος καὶ ἄσπιλος, ἐν ᾗ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατῴκησεν. 8. ἔχεις καὶ ταύτης τῆς παραβολῆς τὴν ἐπίλυσιν.

translation.text:
He says[1], “I told you just now that you are crafty and headstrong, asking for the interpretations of the parables. But since you are so persistent, I will interpret for you the parable of the field and the rest. He entrusted them to the angels to keep them; and he himself cleansed their sins, having labored much and endured many toils—for no one can dig without toil or labor.

Therefore[2], having cleansed the sins of the people, he showed them the paths of life, giving them the law that he received from his Father. “You see,” he says, “that he himself is Lord of the people, having received all authority from his Father. And as for the Lord’s taking his Son and the glorious angels as counselors concerning the inheritance of the servant—listen.

The Holy Spirit, which preexisted, which created all creation, God caused to dwell in flesh that he willed. This flesh, then, in which the Holy Spirit dwelt, served the Spirit well, walking in modesty and purity, in no way at all defiling the Spirit. Therefore, since it had conducted itself well and purely, and had toiled together with the Spirit and cooperated in every matter, conducting itself strongly and courageously, he chose it as a partner with the Holy Spirit; for the conduct of this flesh pleased [the Lord], because it was not defiled upon the earth while having the Holy Spirit.

Therefore he took the Son and the glorious angels as counselors, in order that this flesh also, having served the Spirit blamelessly, might have some place of dwelling, and might not seem to have lost the reward of its service. For every flesh that is found undefiled and unstained, in which the Holy Spirit has dwelt, will receive a reward[b][a][4][3]. You have the interpretation of this parable also.”

footnotes.text: The Greek at this point in our OCR is damaged. Many editions read that the Lord ‘entrusted them to the angels to keep them.’ We translate accordingly.
‘Dig’ renders σκάφεῦσαι, keeping the field/labor metaphor active in the parable.
‘The Holy Spirit, which pre‑existed’ translates τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ προόν. Alternatives include ‘the pre‑existent Holy Spirit’ or ‘the holy pre‑existent Spirit.’
‘Place of dwelling’ renders τόπον τινὰ κατασκηνώσεως, an image of a settled abode; it anticipates reward imagery (‘wage’) in what follows.

Or '‘You see,’ he says, ‘that he himself is Lord of the people, having received all authority from his Father. And that the Lord took his Son and the glorious angels as counselor concerning the inheritance of the slave—listen.'.
Or 'Therefore he took the Son and the glorious angels as counselor,'.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Negative moral nuance in Hermas; ‘crafty’ conveys guile rather than prudence.
Captures willful stubbornness without overreading as arrogance.
Technical term for explaining parables; ‘interpretation’ is standard.
Hermas uses ‘parable’ language; avoid flattening to ‘allegory’.
Neutral-to-firm sense fits the shepherd’s tone without pejorative overload.
Basic agricultural image; ‘field’ matches the parable setting.
Articular infinitive of purpose; ‘keep’ is concise while preserving the sense of safeguarding.
Agrarian metaphor; ‘dig’ is idiomatic and vivid.
Pairing preserves the intensifying repetition in Greek.
‘Paths’ retains the concrete metaphor and traditional idiom.
Given ‘received from his Father,’ the giving of a ‘law’ fits Hermas’s moral-torah motif.
Covenantal title in Christian usage; context indicates exalted authority.
Idiomatic rendering of taking someone as a counselor.
Legal/moral nuance of what is received; consistent with Hermas’s usage.
Per project policy, retain the bonded status where salient in the parable.

lexical_decisions.source_word: τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ προόν
lexical_decisions.rationale: Relative clause keeps Greek structure and highlights pre-existence.
Preserves agency of God and the indwelling concept.
Literal sense maintained; Hermas contrasts ‘flesh’ with ‘Spirit’.
Early Christian virtue tone; pairs well with ‘purity’.
General moral purity suits the broader context beyond sexual chastity.
Cultic/moral defilement language preserved.
Keeps behavioral connotation without idiomatic smoothing.
Preserves the cooperative toil motif with the Spirit.
Straightforward rendering of collaborative action.
‘Courage’ captures ἀνδρείως without archaic ‘manfully’.
Conveys shared participation with the Holy Spirit.
Reflects the editorial note in Greek and clarifies the implied subject.
‘Dwelling’ fits the eschatological settling motif better than ‘encampment’ in English.
Labor imagery (‘toil, dig’) is active; ‘wage’ preserves the metaphor.
Standard rendering for receiving a due or reward.
Pairs two purity terms without collapsing nuance.
Consistency with earlier use.

theological_decisions.issue: Christology: ‘the Holy Spirit, which pre‑existed … God made to dwell in flesh’
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render the clauses as written, preserving the distinction between the pre‑existent Holy Spirit and ‘the flesh’ that served it, without harmonizing to later Trinitarian formulae.
alternative_readings: Interpret ‘Holy Spirit’ here as ‘Son of God’ and paraphrase accordingly
Conflate ‘Spirit’ and ‘flesh’ into a single subject to avoid perceived adoptionism
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas’s idiom identifies the ‘Son of God’ with the Spirit elsewhere and speaks of the Spirit indwelling flesh; the translation keeps this tension rather than smoothing it doctrinally.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy: Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.

theological_decisions.issue: Reference of ‘Lord’ in v.4 (‘he himself is Lord of the people’)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: In context, ‘he’ refers to the Son, who ‘received all authority from his Father.’
theological_decisions.rationale: The relative clause ‘having received all authority from his Father’ best fits the Son as subject.
Per Cartha policy, where bonded status is salient in an inheritance/custody parable, ‘slave’ is the most transparent rendering.
The phrase ‘gave them the law which he received from his Father’ evokes a comprehensive moral rule rather than a single command; ‘law’ preserves the weight.

theological_decisions.issue: Subject of ‘he chose it as partner with the Holy Spirit’ (v.6)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Subject is God (‘[the Lord]’), object is the flesh; hence, ‘he [the Lord] chose it [the flesh] as partner with the Holy Spirit.’
alternative_readings: The Spirit chose the flesh as partner
The flesh chose the Spirit as partner
theological_decisions.rationale: The immediately following clause ‘for the course of this flesh pleased [the Lord]’ supports God as subject; editorial bracket in Greek also points this way.

review_passes.summary: The draft is generally strong but contains a few syntactical missteps and missing conjunctions. A relative pronoun was translated as an adverb ('as he willed' instead of 'that he willed'), a misplaced modifier made it sound like the 'wage' was undefiled rather than the 'flesh', and the present tense φησί was rendered as past. Additionally, two instances of οὖν were skipped, and the translation of σύμβουλον ἔλαβε was harmonized for consistency.
issues_found: Mistranslation: 'He said' for φησί (present tense 'he says').
Lexical choice: 'expended many toils' for ἠντληκώς. The verb ἀντλέω metaphorically means to endure or suffer; 'endured' is more accurate.
Consistency: σύμβουλον ἔλαβε is translated 'took... into counsel' in v.4 but 'took... as counselor' in v.7. Harmonized to 'as counselor' in both places.
Mistranslation: 'in flesh as he willed' for εἰς σάρκα ἣν ἠβούλετο. The relative pronoun ἣν refers to the flesh ('flesh that he willed'), not an adverbial 'as'.
Missing words: οὖν is untranslated in v.5 ('This flesh, then...') and v.6 ('Therefore, having conducted itself...').

Awkward English / Misplaced modifier: 'every flesh will receive a wage that is found undefiled' makes it sound like the wage is undefiled. Restructured to 'every flesh that is found undefiled... will receive a wage'.

revisions.from: ‘You see,’ he says, ‘that he himself is Lord of the people, having received all authority from his Father. And that the Lord took his Son and the glorious angels as counselor concerning the inheritance of the slave—listen.
revisions.to: “You see,” he says, “that he himself is Lord of the people, having received all authority from his Father. And that the Lord took his Son and the glorious angels as counselors concerning the inheritance of the slave—listen.
revisions.rationale: The text is already inside a continuous double-quoted speech by the shepherd; the narrator's φησίν ("he says") should interrupt the double quotes rather than using single quotes (which are also left unclosed in the draft). Additionally, because the object of "took" is plural ("his Son and the glorious angels"), the object complement σύμβουλον should be rendered as the plural "counselors" in English to avoid grammatical discord. | Adjudicator: The proposed rewrite correctly resolves two issues. First, it fixes the punctuation by replacing the unclosed single quotes with double quotes, properly formatting the narrator's interruption (φησίν)

revisions.from: Therefore he took the Son and the glorious angels as counselor,
revisions.to: Therefore he took the Son and the glorious angels as counselors,
revisions.rationale: As above, the plural compound object ("the Son and the glorious angels") requires a plural object complement ("counselors") in English, even though the Greek σύμβουλον is singular (functioning as a collective role). | Adjudicator: The Greek uses the singular σύμβουλον (counselor) to denote the collective advisory role, but in English grammar, a plural compound object ('the Son and the glorious angels') requires a plural object

translation.text: The Holy Spirit, which preexisted, which created all creation, God caused to dwell in flesh that he willed. This flesh, then, in which the Holy Spirit dwelt, served the Spirit well, walking in modesty and purity, in no way at all defiling the Spirit. base_translation.text: He says, “I told you just now that you are crafty and headstrong, asking for the interpretations of the parables. But since you are so persistent, I will interpret for you the parable of the field and the rest. He entrusted them to the angels to keep them; and he himself cleansed their sins, having labored much and endured many toils—for no one can dig without toil or labor.

translation.text: He says, “I just told you that you are crafty and stubborn because you keep asking what the parables mean. But since you will not give up, I will explain the parable of the field and the rest. He entrusted them to the angels for safekeeping. He himself cleansed their sins, working hard and enduring many hardships—for no one can dig without hard work.”

translation.text: The Holy Spirit existed before all things and created everything. God made the Spirit live in the flesh he had chosen. That flesh served the Spirit well. It conducted itself with strength and courage. Therefore, God chose that flesh to be the Holy Spirit’s partner. Its conduct pleased the Lord because, while it had the Holy Spirit, it remained undefiled on earth.

spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft clearly and appropriately simplifies the counselor, participial-service, and interpretation language without importing a doctrinal reading. However, “remains pure” adds a durative condition not expressed by the POB’s “is found undefiled and unstained.” Replacing it with “is found pure and unstained” preserves the criterion while remaining clear for modern readers.

S.5.v.text: Εἶπόν σοι, φησί, καὶ ἄρτι, ὅτι πανοῦργος εἶ καὶ αὐθάδης, ἐπερωτῶν τὰς ἐπιλύσεις τῶν παραβολῶν. ἐπειδὴ δὲ οὕτω παράμονος εἶ, ἐπιλύσω σοι τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ ἀγροῦ καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν τῶν ἀκολούθων πάντων, ἵνα γνωστὰ πάντα ποιήσῃς αὐτά. ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, καὶ σύνιε αὐτά. 2. ὁ ἀγρὸς ὁ κόσμος οὗτός ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ κύριος τοῦ ἀγροῦ, ὁ κτίσας τὰ πάντα καὶ ἀπαρτίσας αὐτὰ καὶ ἐνδυναμώσας. ὁ δὲ δοῦλος ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν· αἱ δὲ ἄμπελοι ὁ λαὸς [οὗτός] ἐστιν ὃν αὐτὸς ἐφύτευσεν. 3. οἱ δὲ χάρακες οἱ [ἅγιοι] ἄγγελοί εἰσιν τοῦ Κυρίου οἱ συγκρατοῦντες τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ· αἱ δὲ βοτάναι αἱ ἐκτετιλμέναι ἐκ τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος, αἱ ἀνομίαι εἰσὶ τῶν δούλων τοῦ Θεοῦ· τὰ δὲ ἐδέσματα ἃ ἔπεμψεν αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ δείπνου, αἱ ἐντολαί εἰσιν ἃς ἔδωκε τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ διὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ· οἱ δὲ φίλοι καὶ σύμβουλοι, οἱ ἅγιοι ἄγγελοι οἱ πρῶτοι κτισθέντες· ἡ δὲ ἀποδημία τοῦ δεσπότου, ὁ χρόνος ὁ περισσεύων εἰς τὴν παρουσίαν αὐτοῦ. 4. λέγω αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μεγάλως καὶ θαυμαστῶς [πάντα ἐστὶ] καὶ ἐνδόξως πάντα ἔχει. μὴ οὖν, φημί, ἐγὼ ἠδυνάμην ταῦτα νοῆσαι; οὐδὲ ἕτερος τῶν ἀνθρώπων, κἂν λίαν συνετός ᾖ τις, οὐ δύναται νοῆσαι αὐτά. ἔτι, φημί, κύριε, δήλωσόν μοι ὃ μέλλω σε ἐπερωτᾶν. 5. Λέγε, φησίν, εἴ τι βούλει. Διατί, φημί, [κύριε,] ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς δούλου τρόπον κεῖται ἐν τῇ παραβολῇ;

S.5.vi.text: Ἄκουε, φησίν· εἰς δούλου τρόπον οὐ κεῖται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἀλλ᾽ εἰς ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην κεῖται καὶ κυριότητα. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε; οὐ νοῶ. 2. Ὅτι, φησίν, ὁ Θεὸς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἐφύτευσε, τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι τὸν λαὸν ἔκτισε, καὶ παρέδωκε τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ὁ υἱὸς κατέστησε τοὺς ἀγγέλους ἐπ᾽ αὐτοὺς τοῦ συντηρεῖν αὐτούς· καὶ αὐτὸς τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν ἐκαθάρισε πολλὰ κοπιάσας καὶ πολλοὺς κόπους ἠντληκώς· οὐδεὶς γὰρ δύναται σκαφεῦσαι ἄτερ κόπου ἢ μόχθου. 3. αὐτὸς οὖν καθαρίσας τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς τρίβους τῆς ζωῆς, δοὺς αὐτοῖς τὸν νόμον ὃν ἔλαβε παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ. 4. | βλέπεις, φησίν, ὅτι αὐτὸς κύριός ἐστι τοῦ λαοῦ, ἐξουσίαν πᾶσαν λαβὼν παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ. | ὅτι δὲ ὁ κύριος σύμβουλον ἔλαβε τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἐνδόξους ἀγγέλους περὶ τῆς κληρονομίας τοῦ δούλου, ἄκουε. 5. τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τὸ προόν, τὸ κτίσαν πᾶσαν τὴν κτίσιν, κατῴκισεν ὁ Θεὸς εἰς σάρκα ἣν ἠβούλετο. αὕτη οὖν ἡ σάρξ, ἐν ᾗ κατῴκησε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἐδούλευσε τῷ πνεύματι καλῶς ἐν σεμνότητι καὶ ἁγνείᾳ πορευθεῖσα, μηδὲν ὅλως μιάνασα τὸ πνεῦμα. 6. πολιτευσαμένην οὖν αὐτὴν καλῶς καὶ ἁγνῶς καὶ συγκοπιάσασαν τῷ πνεύματι καὶ συνεργήσασαν ἐν παντὶ πράγματι, ἰσχυρῶς καὶ ἀνδρείως ἀναστραφεῖσαν, μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου εἵλατο κοινωνόν· ἤρεσε γὰρ [τῷ Κυρίῳ] ἡ πορεία τῆς σαρκὸς ταύτης, ὅτι οὐκ ἐμιάνθη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔχουσα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον. 7. σύμβουλον οὖν ἔλαβε τὸν υἱὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοὺς ἐνδόξους, ἵνα καὶ ἡ σὰρξ αὕτη, δουλεύσασα τῷ πνεύματι ἀμέμπτως, σχῇ τόπον τινὰ κατασκηνώσεως, καὶ μὴ δόξῃ τὸν μισθὸν | τῆς δουλείας αὐτῆς ἀπολωλεκέναι· πᾶσα γὰρ σὰρξ ἀπολήψεται μισθὸν | ἡ εὑρεθεῖσα ἀμίαντος καὶ ἄσπιλος, ἐν ᾗ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατῴκησεν. 8. ἔχεις καὶ ταύτης τῆς παραβολῆς τὴν ἐπίλυσιν.
